REVIEW: FLAVORS OF GROWTH

• SGP accommodates both Norm- and Criterion-Referenced growth

 • Norm-Referenced: Cohort referenced SGPs

 • Criterion-Referenced: Baseline referenced/anchored SGPs, student growth projections/targets
 (i.e., growth to standard), catch-up/keep-up/move-up/stay-up.

• Based upon state preference, policy, and data, different states have created
 different combinations of norm- and criterion-referenced growth metrics.

• These growth metrics often have different data requirements.

• SGP calculation is robust to scale transformations. It unlikely that the transition
 from a state assessment scale to a SBAC scale will prevent the calculation of an
 SGP. However, this has to be validated on a state by state, content area by
 content area, and grade by grade basis.

REVIEW: THREATS TO CALCULATION

• SGPs don’t require a vertical scale for calculation (which SBAC has by design).
 SGPs can be calculated using both vertical and non-vertical scales.

• A significant ceiling/floor associated with a test (either SBAC or a state test
 used as a prior) can lead to bad model fit. These growth metrics often have
 different data requirements.

• Barring significant ceiling/floor, norm-referenced analyses will very likely yield a
 uniform distribution of percentiles.

• SGP calculation is robust to scale transformations. It unlikely that the transition
 from a state assessment scale to a SBAC scale will prevent the calculation of an
 SGP. However, this has to be validated on a state by state, content area by
 content area, and grade by grade basis.

REVIEW: REQUIREMENTS FOR CALCULATING
GROWTH: SGP
• Annual growth? Bi-annual growth? Tri-annual growth?

• Annual growth (norm-referenced SGPs based upon a single cohort) requires
 (at a minimum) two consecutive annual measures (i.e., scale scores) of student
 achievement (usually taken from the same content area).

• Annual growth (anchored/baseline-referenced SGPs) requires (at a minimum)
 two consecutive annual measures (i.e., scale scores) of student achievement
 (usually taken from the same content area) from the same assessment (i.e., an
 assessment with a time-invariant scale).

• Annual targets (SGP Projections/Targets/Trajectories) require (at a minimum)
 two consecutive annual measures of student achievement from the same
 assessment (i.e., an assessment with a time-invariant scale).

REVIEW: REQUIREMENTS FOR CALCULATING
GROWTH: SGP
• States primarily focus on annual growth, particularly for accountability
 (exceptions include, for example, student growth from 8th to 10th grade).

• SBAC field testing will impact a state’s ability to calculate growth for students due
 to the simple fact that student will not receive back scale scores on the SBAC
 field test.

• Absent double testing, students participating in the field test cannot receive
 annual SGPs in BOTH 2013-2014 (no current year score) AND 2014-2015 (no
 prior year score).

• If a student has a scale score in 2012-2013, one could, for example, calculate a
 two year SGP for a students participating in field testing between 2012-2013 and
 2014-2015.

• In the years after the transition, absent double testing, students will have different
 numbers of priors available for SGP analyses.

REVIEW: REQUIREMENTS FOR CALCULATING
GROWTH: SUMMARY

• Easier to conduct norm-referenced SGP analyses during transition than
 criterion-referenced growth to standard analyses.

• Criterion-referenced projections require linking SGP analyses done exclusively
 on the SBAC assessment in order to extrapolate forward how much growth is
 required to, for example catch-up/keep-up/move-up/stay-up.

• Analogously growth-to-standard (e.g., career and college-readiness) will require
 at least two years data on the new scale as well as fixed achievement levels/
 standards defined on the new scale.

• Establishing baseline referenced SGPs will likely require even more time (e.g., 4
 years) to establish a stable baseline from which to compare going forward.

REQUIREMENTS FOR THE USE OF GROWTH
• Two distinct challenges: Calculation and Use

• Just because we can calculate an SGP doesn’t mean it is defensible to use it for
 previously existing accountability purposes.

• Validating SGP use will require defining the purpose.

• Current state uses include:

 • Teacher evaluation (required by RttT, ESEA waiver, state policy/rule
 making, ...)

 • School and District accountability (ESEA waiver, state policy, ...)

 • Charter school accreditation.

REQUIREMENTS FOR THE USE OF GROWTH

• During the assessment transition, a number of challenges confront states using
 growth for accountability purposes.

 • Data time span (e.g., two-year growth) not aligned with accountability time
 span (annual)

 • Changes in types of growth analyses done for accountability during transition.
 Criterion-referenced growth not available until year 2 of SBAC.

 • Assessment results from different assessments (state and SBAC). Depending
 upon the number of priors used by the state, this will be an ongoing issue
 for many years.

 • Missing data due to SBAC field testing.

REQUIREMENTS FOR THE USE OF GROWTH
 • Data time span (e.g., two-year growth) not aligned with accountability time
 span (annual)

 • Most accountability systems use an observational pre-post design to hold
 teachers/schools/districts accountable.

 • Often, the pre-test occurs the spring prior to enrollment in the unit of
 accountability and the post-test the spring during enrollment.

 • An extended growth time span (e.g., two-year) undermines the attribution
 of responsibility implicit within the accountability determination.

 • Misfit between accountability and growth time span impact school and
 district accountability as well, but likely will have less impact because field
 testing does not occur school wide.
